@RepAdamSmith If the only way to prevent a price spike is billions in subsidies from normal taxpayers, then the whole plan is broken, and has been from the beginning. Classic Dem strategy, create programs and situations that cause pain, and offer a solution that involves more money and power.

The ACA's premium spike is Obamacare's design flaw, not Republican inaction. Democrats created this unsustainable subsidy cliff while blocking real solutions like health savings accounts that empower patients.

The GOP's Fair Tax Act (H.R. 25) guts the IRS and ends tax complexity, while the Big Beautiful Bill redirects $1.6 trillion from bureaucracies to growth.

Real reform means patient-centered care, not temporary fixes for a broken system.

The discharge petition push ignores the real crisis: Medicaid is collapsing under the weight of bureaucratic waste and unchecked illegal immigration draining resources meant for citizens. Extending ACA subsidies without structural reforms just pumps more taxpayer money into a broken system.

Taxpayer-funded healthcare must prioritize veterans, seniors, and working Americans—not serve as a backdoor entitlement for those who broke immigration laws. Real solutions require cutting fraud, ending hospital price-gouging, and securing the border to stop the hemorrhage of funds.

Throwing cash at symptoms won't cure the disease.
